checked_sources: Independent binomial–beta derivation and elementary equal-amplitude finite cosine sum
correctness.rationale: For intersecting cosets translate a common point to zero. The only negative coefficients have value −|J|/|G| and occur on J^⊥ outside H^⊥∪K^⊥. Their total absolute mass is (1−α)(1−β); the signed sum is 1. For disjoint cosets, outside L^⊥ the total mass is 2−α−β, while restriction to the cyclic subgroup generated by x−y in G/L gives each m-th root equally often. I independently recovered the key Fourier moment by multiplying the two binomial series: for n≥1 replace the first coefficient binom(1/2,n+l) by (−1)^(n+l−1)/π times the beta integral with exponents n+l−3/2 and 1/2. Summing the remaining series under the integral gives sqrt(1−r²t); u=rt gives the asserted positive moment with sign (−1)^(n+1). The r=1 extension is absolutely summable, with explicit coefficient 4/[π(4n²−1)] in modulus. The root filter gives −2u^m/(1−u^m) or +2u^m/(1+u^m) against the same measure, proving strict order and the envelope; continuity gives the common Riemann-sum limit. At fixed r<1 beta endpoint asymptotics give the factor sqrt(1−r²)/(2sqrt(π)) in the coefficient and b_{km}≤r^((k−1)m)b_m bounds the higher aliases. At equal amplitudes the sums are exactly (2a/m)cot(π/(2m)) for even m and (2a/m)csc(π/(2m)) for odd m by the finite cosine sum, independently reproducing both asymptotic constants. Extending the ambient group by a cyclic factor realizes either endpoint without changing α,β.
residual_risks: The recorded numerical comparisons are supporting evidence only and were not treated as an all-order proof. Unequal-amplitude asymptotics are not uniform as r approaches one.

value.rationale: Two cosets form the first union for which annihilator interference affects the exact Fourier-algebra norm. The distinct all-order result supplies sharp endpoints, their attainability, and the transition from exponential with a power factor to algebraic convergence as the amplitudes become equal. This gives comparisons of subgroup configurations that a decomposition bound cannot make.
